arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Justice Scalia questioned the link between car emissions and state injury.
Justice Kennedy asked if proving global warming is necessary for standing.
The EPA argued Congress did not authorize greenhouse gas regulation.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests whether the EPA must regulate carbon dioxide from cars. The states claim this pollution harms them. The agency says its law does not cover this issue.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Massachusetts wants the Court to order the EPA to set car emission limits.
The EPA wants the Court to dismiss the case for lack of standing.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Massachusetts argues the EPA has the legal duty to regulate vehicle emissions.
